issuer: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Consular Affairs (Passport Services)

fee.feeBasis: First-time adult (16+) passport book on Form DS-11: $130 application fee paid to the Department of State plus $35 facility acceptance fee paid to the acceptance facility. Two separate payments.

renewalFeeNote: Adult renewal by mail/online on Form DS-82: $130 application fee only; no acceptance fee.
expediteFeeNote: Paid per application on top of required fees. Optional 1-3 day return delivery of the issued book is a further $23.36 (U.S. mailing addresses only).

expediteDays.note: Stated as 2-3 weeks, not including mailing.

processingDays.note: Routine stated as 4-6 weeks. The Department states processing begins the day the application is received at a passport agency or center and does not include mailing times, which may add several weeks.

childValidityNote: Under 16: $100 application + $35 acceptance fee; valid 5 years and cannot be renewed by mail.

lostReplacement.note: Report on Form DS-64 (online reports are cancelled within 1 business day). In the U.S., a replacement must be applied for in person on Form DS-11, which carries the first-time fees ($130 + $35). Once reported, the passport is no longer valid and cannot be used for international travel even if found later; travelling on it can lead to detention on entry.

minRemainingValidityNote: The Department warns that some foreign destinations require at least 6 months of validity beyond the trip, and some airlines will not board passengers who do not meet it.
abroadNote: Outside the U.S. (except Canada) citizens apply at the nearest U.S. embassy or consulate, pay the passport fee only, and do not pay the expedite fee. Residents of Canada may mail a renewal to the U.S. with routine or expedited service.

issuer: Department of Foreign Affairs – Passport Service (An Roinn Gnóthaí Eachtracha)

fee.feeBasis: Standard adult 10-year passport via Passport Online; the same €75 applies to a first-time adult application and to a renewal. Post Passport (paper) channel: €80 plus a postal service fee of €9.50 per single application (€16 for up to four sent together). Public-counter renewal in Dublin/Cork: €95 passport fee plus an appointment fee. Passport Card €35; book plus card bundle €100. Applicants living outside Ireland pay an extra €15 postal fee when applying online. Expedite: Adult renewals only, never first-time applications, by booked appointment at the public offices. Same-day turnaround (Dublin): €95 passport fee plus €150 appointment fee, €245 in total. Four-day turnaround (Cork and Dublin): €95 plus €75, €170 in total. London offers a five-day turnaround at €170. The page does not say whether 'four-day' means working or calendar days. A same-day emergency service for bereavement or medical emergency charges only the passport fee.

processingDays.note: Average Passport Online turnaround, converted from working days at x7/5: simple adult renewal 10 working days = 14 calendar days; complex adult renewal (lost or stolen passport, name change, extra documents) 15 working days = 21; first-time adult online application 20 working days = 28. Post Passport (paper) and Passport Assist take about 6 weeks = 42 days. The times exclude postage both ways and start only when any supporting documents arrive. First-time applications cannot be expedited.

childValidityNote: Children under 18 get a 5-year passport. Online fee €20 plus a €5 postal fee, or €15 postal if living outside Ireland; paper €30.

lostReplacement.note: The loss is reported inside the replacement application, which is handled as a complex renewal (15 working days). The fee schedule lists no separate fee for a lost passport, so the standard €75 online fee applies. DFA reports the lost passport to Interpol and it is no longer valid for travel, even if it is later found. Losing two or more passports in 10 years can restrict the next passport to between 1 and 10 years' validity. Adults whose last passport was lost or stolen need extra identity verification (a Public Services Card, or other documents or an interview).

minRemainingValidityNote: DFA's guidance: as a rule of thumb keep six months' validity beyond the date you return home, and check the destination's embassy; travel within the EU is possible right up to expiry. An online renewal can be made when the passport expires within the next 12 months. A current passport with more than 12 months left must be sent in with the application.
abroadNote: Passport Online works from anywhere in the world at the same €75 adult fee, plus a €15 postal fee for applicants living outside Ireland. Turnaround times are the same regardless of residence, but postage from abroad is longer. First-time applicants abroad have their identity form witnessed by an appropriate witness outside the State rather than An Garda Síochána. Where local post is unreliable, documents go through the nearest Irish Embassy. The Irish Embassy in London runs a five-day urgent renewal service at €170. Fees for other embassy-lodged applications were not checked.

issuer: Þjóðskrá Íslands (Registers Iceland), which produces and issues the passport; applications are taken by the Sýslumenn (District Commissioners) in Iceland and by Icelandic embassies abroad

fee.feeBasis: Standard processing (almenn afgreiðsla), adults aged 18 to 66. The same price applies to a first passport and a renewal. Apply online on Ísland.is or at a Sýslumaður office, then attend photographing in person within 30 days. Children, people aged 67 and over, and disability pensioners pay 7,000 ISK. Expedite: 39,200 ISK is the full price of express processing (hraðafgreiðsla) for ages 18 to 66, not a surcharge on top of the standard fee. It is 14,000 ISK for children, people aged 67 and over, and disability pensioners. Express delivery is within 2 days of the photographing appointment. The page does not say whether these are working days, so the figure is not converted.

processingDays.note: Registers Iceland: processing takes up to 4 working days from receipt of the application, excluding weekends and holidays. 4 working days x7/5 = 5.6, rounded to 6 calendar days. The Sýslumenn page says standard delivery is within 4 days of the photographing appointment. Shipping time is added for applicants outside the capital area and for delivery abroad. No minimum is stated.

childValidityNote: Valid 10 years from the application date; 5 years for children under 18.

lostReplacement.note: A passport reported lost is entered in the Schengen and Interpol systems and becomes permanently unusable. If found, it must be handed in, and one presented abroad is confiscated. The replacement is given the same validity end date as the passport reported lost (Passports Act art. 6(2)). Anyone who has lost two or more passports may get a passport valid 2 years or less while the lost ones remain valid (Regulation art. 18). No separate replacement fee is published.

minRemainingValidityNote: Registers Iceland's general guidance: most EEA/Schengen states require the travel document to be valid at least 3 months beyond the planned stay; many non-EEA states require at least 6 months, some longer. Online application is only possible when the current passport has 9 months or less left; with more than 9 months left, you must apply in person at a Sýslumaður.
abroadNote: Abroad, applications are taken only at certain Icelandic embassies and consulates-general. Honorary consuls can issue only emergency passports, not ordinary ones. Bring the old passport, or photo ID if it was lost, and payment. Delivery options are collection at the application post or DHL shipping abroad, and shipping time is added. The fee charged at embassies was not found on the pages checked.

issuer: Passbehörde der Gemeinde (Bürgeramt), passport produced centrally by Bundesdruckerei GmbH; abroad: deutsche Auslandsvertretung (Auswärtiges Amt)

fee.feeBasis: Standard 32-page Reisepass for an applicant who has completed their 24th year (24+), issued by the competent domestic Passbehörde; same fee for first issue and renewal (PassV § 27(1) Nr. 1a). Under 24: 37.50 EUR. Surcharges: 48 pages +22 EUR; photo taken at the office +6 EUR; direct postal delivery (Direktversand) +15 EUR; fee doubled at a non-competent authority (PassV § 27(2) Nr. 2).

processingDays.note: Berlin's official service page states 'bis zu 8 Wochen' (up to 8 weeks = 56 days) for a standard passport, collected in person at the Bürgeramt unless the optional 15 EUR Direktversand (pilot) is chosen. expediteFee 32 is the Express SURCHARGE (PassV § 27(1) Nr. 1d), so an adult Express passport totals 102 EUR. Express: 'In der Regel 4 Werktage' if applied for by 11:00 (Berlin); BMI states the passport is generally available by the third working day after transmission to the manufacturer by 12:00. expediteDays converts 4 working days to 4-6 calendar days depending on intervening weekend. Vorläufiger Reisepass (no chip, max 1 year validity, PassG § 5(3); only when even Express is too late): 26 EUR (PassV § 27(1) Nr. 1e), issued immediately ('Bearbeitungsdauer sofort').

childValidityNote: PassG § 5(1): 10 years; 6 years for persons who have not completed their 24th year (i.e. all under-24s, children included). Passport validity cannot be extended (§ 5(4)). Vorläufiger Reisepass max 1 year (§ 5(3)). Kinderreisepass not covered here.

lostReplacement.note: Loss must be reported to the Passbehörde without delay (PassG § 15 Nr. 3); replacement is a new passport at the ordinary fee (70 EUR for 24+). The lost passport is entered in the national search database (and Interpol); official guidance advises not to travel on a recovered passport even after reporting its recovery, as the Interpol entry is not automatically deleted and border police may seize it. 'oldCancelled' reflects this search-entry practice; PassG § 11 does not list loss as a ground of automatic invalidity.

minRemainingValidityNote: No German rule; remaining-validity requirements are set by the destination country (Auswärtiges Amt travel advice).
abroadNote: Residents abroad apply in person at the competent German mission (Auslandsvertretung); fees rise by 36 EUR (PassV § 27(3)): 106 EUR for 24+, 73.50 EUR under 24; at a non-competent mission 176 EUR / 111 EUR. Vorläufiger Reisepass abroad 75 EUR (26+49), 101 EUR at non-competent mission. Honorary consuls add 73.13-88.43 EUR plus expenses. Processing 4-6 weeks because the passport travels Bundesdruckerei -> Auswärtiges Amt Berlin -> mission; Express shortens only production time. A lost passport abroad can be replaced by a Reiseausweis als Passersatz for return to Germany (max 1 month).

fee.feeBasis: Timbre fiscal for an adult (18+) passport, metropolitan France, first application or renewal alike (43 EUR in Guyane). Minors: 42 EUR aged 15-17, 17 EUR aged 0-14. If the photo is taken at the counter (only where no professional photographer), the stamp is 89 EUR.

processingDays.note: Service-public gives no fixed figure: the passport is not made on site, 'il faut compter plusieurs semaines' and times depend on place and season (longer before summer holidays). It must be collected in person at the place of application within 3 months or it is destroyed. There is no paid express service for the regular passport; expediteFee 30 is the timbre fiscal for a 'passeport temporaire' (urgent passport, valid 1 year) granted by the prefecture only for medical, humanitarian or unpostponable professional reasons; it may be handed over immediately or take a few days (hence expediteDays min 0, max not stated).

childValidityNote: Adult passport valid 10 years; a minor's passport is valid 5 years (can still be used after turning 18 until expiry). Minor fee: 17 EUR ages 0-14, 42 EUR ages 15-17. Passeport temporaire valid 1 year.

lostReplacement.note: Replacement after loss costs the ordinary 86 EUR stamp (96 EUR abroad); the loss declaration (cerfa n°14011) can be made at the time of the new application. Once loss or theft is declared the passport is invalidated in the computer systems, irreversibly, and reported to Interpol and the Schengen Information System; a found passport must be returned to a prefecture.

abroadNote: Abroad the adult passport costs 96 EUR (minors 27 EUR 0-14, 52 EUR 15-17), applied for at the embassy/consulate; the passeport temporaire costs 90 EUR. Residents registered on the Registre des Français établis hors de France can request postal delivery (prepaid envelope via the consulate's approved carrier). In Australia, Canada, Spain and Portugal eligible adults can renew without visiting the consulate.

fee.feeBasis: Single tasa for first issue, renewal, loss, theft, early renewal ('anticipo') or damage, any age: 30,00 EUR; free for holders of a valid Título de Familia Numerosa. Amount set annually by the Ley de Presupuestos Generales del Estado.

childValidityNote: RD 896/2003 art. 6: 10 years if the holder is 30 or older at issue; 5 years if under 30; 2 years if under 5. Minors under 14 resident in Spain without a DNI: valid at most until age 14, never over 5 years. Validity is non-extendable.

lostReplacement.note: Same 30 EUR tasa. Loss/theft must be reported immediately to police/Guardia Civil (or consulate abroad). abroadNote: Only Spaniards registered as residents in the consulate's Registro de Matrícula Consular can get an ordinary passport abroad; the consular tasa is also 30 EUR. It is not issued on the spot: consular pages cite an indicative average of about 3 weeks. Non-registered Spaniards who lost their passport abroad can be issued a pasaporte provisional (RD 896/2003).

issuer: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan (外務省), with applications taken and passports issued through prefectural passport offices (e.g. 東京都生活文化局 旅券課 / Tokyo Passport Centres)

fee.feeBasis: 10-year passport, applicant 18 or over, window (paper) application in Japan, new or renewal (切替) alike. Made of 7,000 national fee (収入印紙 revenue stamp) + 2,300 prefectural fee (Tokyo). Online application via Mynaportal: 8,900 (7,000 stamp + 1,900 prefectural; the prefectural fee is 400 lower online). Applies to applications from 2026-07-01. Before 2026-07-01 the 10-year fee was 16,300 window (14,000 stamp + 2,300 prefectural) / 15,900 online, and a 5-year passport for 12+ was 11,300 (9,000 + 2,300). From 2026-07-01 the 5-year passport is only for under-18s (4,800 window: 2,500 + 2,300; 4,400 online); adults can only get 10-year. A same-remaining-validity replacement (残存有効期間同一旅券, 18+) is 5,800 window (3,500 + 2,300). If a previously issued passport lapsed uncollected (未交付失効) within the last 5 years, the 10-year fee is 15,300 (11,000 + 4,300). The 2025 changes: from 2025-03-24 all passport applications (not only renewals) can be made online via Mynaportal, with the 400-yen-lower prefectural fee online.

processingDays.note: Tokyo: collection from the 9th business day at the earliest (最短で9営業日目), excluding Saturdays, Sundays, public holidays and 29 Dec - 3 Jan; the delivery date can slip. 9 business days converted to roughly 10-12 calendar days depending on the weekday of application; min 10 given. No official maximum stated. The applicant must collect in person at the passport centre (no mail delivery), and must collect within 6 months of issue or the passport lapses. Other prefectures set their own lead times. Applications at overseas missions take about 1 month (around 2 weeks longer than in Japan, because the passport is shipped from Japan).

validityNote: From 2026-07-01 anyone 18 or over at the date of application receives a 10-year passport; the adult 5-year option was withdrawn. Before 2026-07-01 adults could choose 5 or 10 years (under-20s were limited to 5 years). A reduced-fee passport with the same remaining validity as the old one is available for 18+ (e.g. when visa pages run out or name changes).
childValidityNote: Under 18 at the date of application: 5-year passport only (4,800 window / 4,400 online, from 2026-07-01). Before 2026-07-01 the 5-year fee was 11,300 for ages 12+ and 6,300 for under 12.

lostReplacement.note: No separate lost-passport fee: the holder files a 紛失一般旅券等届出書 (loss report, in person or online since 2025-03-24) and applies for a new passport at the ordinary fee (9,300 window / 8,900 online for 18+). Filing the report invalidates the lost passport; MOFA publishes its number in the official gazette (官報) and notifies foreign authorities, and it cannot be used even if found. A police report reference (or fire/municipal disaster certificate) is required. Alternative: a same-remaining-validity passport (5,800 window) is available for 18+.

minRemainingValidityNote: Japan allows a renewal (切替申請) once remaining validity is under 1 year, or when visa pages are down to 3 spreads or fewer; with 1 year or more left, applicants going on long postings/study are told to consult the passport office. Online renewal is not accepted when 1 year or more remains (except for the page and name-change cases). The new passport discards the old one's remaining validity.
abroadNote: Residents abroad apply at a Japanese embassy or consulate. The fee is charged in local currency at a rate each mission publishes (set by fiscal-year exchange rates), and the 2026-07-01 reduction applies from 00:00 Japan time (or the same clock time locally for missions behind Japan). Processing is about 1 month because passports are produced in Japan and shipped. Local-currency amounts are on each mission's site and were not collected here.

issuer: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (외교부 여권과), through passport agencies (여권사무 대행기관: provincial/city halls and district offices) and overseas missions

fee.feeBasis: 10-year multiple-entry electronic passport (복수여권), 58 pages, applicant 18 or over; first issue and reissue alike. Made of 40,000 passport issuance fee (여권발급수수료) + 12,000 international exchange contribution (국제교류기여금). 26-page version: 49,000 (37,000 + 12,000). Issuance fee rose by 2,000 won from 2026-03-01. At overseas missions: USD 52 (58p) / USD 49 (26p).

processingDays.note: The passport.go.kr pages fetched do not state a standard processing time. District offices publish their own: Seocho-gu says 8+ business days from application to collection and possibly 10-11 business days at busy times; Jungnang-gu says 10 business days including the application day; Gwanak-gu says 7-8 business days plus possible 2-3 days' delay. Converted using Seocho's 8-11 business days to about 10-15 calendar days. Figures confirmed only through search snippets of those official district pages (the pages themselves did not load). Collection is in person; an optional postal-delivery service adds about 3-4 business days (up to 10+ in some areas). Expedite: the 48-hour electronic passport (48시간내 발급여권) is charged the ordinary fee (52,000 / 49,000) but only granted on strict criteria (a family emergency abroad, humanitarian or urgent business need, or an agency error found just before departure), applied for before 14:00 at a domestic agency; if refused it follows the normal timeline. Separately, an emergency passport (긴급여권: non-electronic, single-journey, valid 1 year) costs 50,000 (USD 50), or 17,000 (USD 17) with proof of a relative's death or critical illness (33,000 refundable if proof is supplied within 6 months); issued at Incheon/Gimhae airport offices and listed city/provincial/district offices.

validityNote: Under Passport Act Enforcement Decree art. 6, anyone 18 or over applying for a multiple passport receives a 10-year passport; no choice of period. Choice of 58 or 26 pages. A single-use passport (단수여권, up to 1 year) costs 17,000 (USD 17). A reissue can instead carry the old passport's remaining validity (남은 유효기간 부여 여권) for 27,000 (USD 27), 58 or 26 pages.
childValidityNote: Under 18: 5-year multiple passport. Ages 8-17: 44,000 (58p; 35,000 + 9,000 contribution) or 41,000 (26p; 32,000 + 9,000). Under 8: 35,000 (58p) or 32,000 (26p), no contribution. A passport of under 5 years' validity (26 pages, e.g. for those with military-service restrictions) costs 17,000.

lostReplacement.note: A lost passport is reported (at a passport agency, via Government24 online, or at a mission abroad) and a new passport is issued at the ordinary fee (52,000 for 10-year 58p, 49,000 for 26p), or with the lost passport's remaining validity for 27,000. A passport reported lost is invalidated immediately, cannot be used even if recovered, and is registered with Interpol. Online reissue is not allowed for repeat losers (2+ losses in 5 years, or 1 loss in 5 years while another valid passport exists).

minRemainingValidityNote: Korea sets no minimum remaining validity for reissue; holders may reissue before expiry at will. passport.go.kr warns that entry rules on remaining validity differ by destination country.
abroadNote: Overseas Koreans apply at a Korean embassy or consulate; fees are charged in US-dollar terms (USD 52 for 10-year 58p, USD 49 for 26p, USD 50 emergency passport). Reissue on expiry can be applied for online through the 재외동포 365 민원포털 (first issue, lost/damaged and data-change cases must apply in person). Passports issued abroad are produced in Korea and shipped, so they take longer than domestic issue (mission-specific times not collected).

issuer: Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores (SRE), through its state offices (oficinas de pasaportes) in Mexico and consular offices abroad

fee.feeBasis: 10-year ordinary passport, adult (18+), first issue or renewal alike, applied for in Mexico; derechos under Ley Federal de Derechos art. 20 fr. IV for 2026 (statutory amount 4,277.69, charged as 4,280). Other adult validities: 3 years 1,795 (art. 20 fr. II, 1,795.29); 6 years 2,440 (fr. III, 2,438.63). 1 year 920 (fr. I, 920.75) is only for children under 3. People over 60 and people with a certified disability pay 50% (3y 900, 6y 1,220, 10y 2,140); agricultural workers under the Mexico-Canada programme pay 50% on 1-6-year passports only. Effective 2026-01-01.

processingDays.note: In Mexico the passport is handed over the same day as the appointment, once requirements are met and the fee is paid. Appointments are booked at citas.sre.gob.mx; waiting time for an appointment is not included and not published. No online application.

childValidityNote: Under 3: 1 or 3 years (the 1-year passport, 920, is only issued to under-3s). Ages 3-17: 3 or 6 years. 10-year validity is for 18+ only. Both parents' (or the legal guardian's) consent is required for under-18s.

lostReplacement.note: No separate replacement fee: after loss, theft or destruction the holder reports it to the Ministerio Público (or the competent foreign authority abroad), fills in the SRE office form, and reapplies with first-time requirements, paying the ordinary fee for the chosen validity (4,280 for 10 years).

minRemainingValidityNote: No minimum: renewal before expiry is allowed, but a person may not hold more than one valid passport, and the current one must be presented at the appointment.
abroadNote: Abroad, Mexicans apply by appointment at a consulate and pay there in US dollars (US figures for 2026, Consulate General in Atlanta): 1 year USD 44, 3 years USD 101, 6 years USD 137, 10 years USD 209; over-60s pay half (USD 50.50 / 68.50 / 104.50). Consulates charge 30% more for an emergency passport (LFD art. 20: USD 57 / 131 / 178 / 272). Fee revenue from abroad funds the consulates.

issuer: Australian Passport Office, Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

fee.feeBasis: Standard adult passport (aged 16 and over, 10-year validity); the same fee applies to a first passport and to a renewal. Figure from the fee table headed 'as of 1 January 2026' - no 1 July 2026 indexation is published; the current schedule is dated 1 January 2026.

processingDays.note: Routine service 'up to 6 weeks' (converted to 42 calendar days), made of up to 5 business days for the application to reach the office, up to 20 business days processing, and up to 5 business days postage; the 6 weeks runs from lodging and paying. No minimum is published. APO reports above 97% available within 6 weeks as at August 2026. Priority ($308 on top of the standard fee): 2 business days processing, 'up to 11 business days' end to end including lodgement transit and postage; expediteDays converts that to 2 (processing only, with collection from a passport office) to 15 calendar days (11 business days). Fast Track ($107 extra): 5 business days processing, up to 14 business days end to end. Faster processing is only available to eligible customers in Australia.

childValidityNote: Child passport for under-16s is 5-year validity, fee $213. Adults aged 75 and over may optionally take a 5-year passport for $213. A passport issued to a child stays valid after they turn 18 until it expires.

lostReplacement.note: A lost or stolen passport must be reported; APO cancels it and it cannot be used again even if found. You must apply for a new passport (not a renewal), so the standard adult fee applies; the $265 'Replacement passport' fee is only for minor damage or a name/gender change and explicitly cannot be used for a lost, stolen or cancelled passport. Two losses in 5 years: next adult passport valid 5 years only, still at the 10-year fee; 3 or more: max 2 years or refusal, still at the 10-year fee. Those with 2+ losses in 5 years are ineligible for faster processing.

minRemainingValidityNote: APO advises avoiding travel outside Australia if the passport expires within the next 6 months, since some countries refuse entry with under 6 months' validity. Renewal requires the old passport to have been issued with at least 2 years' validity, at age 16+, on or after 1 January 2006. Remaining validity does not carry over and the current passport is generally cancelled on renewal.
abroadNote: Apply or renew through an Australian embassy or consulate, paying in local currency the equivalent of the AUD fee plus an overseas surcharge of $189 (adult) or $92 (child). Overseas applications are not eligible for Priority or Fast Track; allow at least 6 weeks, with mailing arrangements depending on location. An emergency passport overseas costs $265 (valid up to one year, no chip).

issuer: Polícia Federal (Departamento de Polícia Federal), Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública

fee.feeBasis: Taxa de emissão de passaporte comum, paid via GRU/PagTesouro after submitting the online form; the same fee applies to first issue and to any new passport (there is no separate renewal). Set by Portaria MJ 927/2015.

processingDays.note: Passport normally ready for collection about 6 business days after the in-person appointment (converted to ~8 calendar days), varying by region since booklets are printed by Casa da Moeda in Rio. Before that: payment clearance (PIX/card 10 min to 24 business hours; boleto 24-72 business hours) and a wait of 1 to 30 days for an appointment. Collected in person at the PF post, not mailed. Reduced-deadline issue, only on documented need (work, study, health; not tourism) and not at every unit, costs R$ 77.17 extra (total R$ 334.42): passaporte de urgência delivered in 3-5 business days, passaporte de emergência within 24 business hours (valid 1 year, not for tourism). expediteDays spans 1 (emergency) to 7 calendar days (5 business days, urgência).

childValidityNote: By age on the day of the appointment: under 1 -> 1 year; 1 to under 2 -> 2 years; 2 to under 3 -> 3 years; 3 to under 4 -> 4 years; 4 to under 18 -> 5 years; 18+ -> 10 years. Emergency passport max 1 year.

lostReplacement.note: If a valid passport was lost, mislaid, destroyed or retained by an embassy/company, a Comunicação de Ocorrência is filed and an additional fee is charged on top of the common R$ 257.25, totalling R$ 514.50 (Portaria MJ 927/2015). If it was stolen or seized and a police report (Boletim de Ocorrência) or seizure record is presented, only the common R$ 257.25 is charged; also only the common fee for loss in a Congress-declared public calamity. A previous passport that is presented is physically cancelled and returned (visas remain valid).

minRemainingValidityNote: Brazil sets no minimum for its own citizens: a passport may be used to leave Brazil up to its last valid day, and to return to Brazil even after expiry. Destination countries may require more (PF cites the Brazilian consulate in Barcelona: at least 3 months beyond departure from Europe). Validity cannot be extended; PF may email a reminder about 8 months before expiry.
abroadNote: Abroad, passports are issued by Brazilian embassies and consulates (Ministério das Relações Exteriores, via e-consular), not the Polícia Federal; fees are the consular fee in local currency, not the GRU. For loss or theft abroad, the holder goes to the Brazilian mission, which issues an Autorização de Retorno if a new passport cannot be issued.

issuer: Te Tari Taiwhenua Department of Internal Affairs (New Zealand Passports)

fee.feeBasis: Standard adult passport (GST inclusive), fee in force from 2 May 2025; the same fee applies to first passports and renewals. Courier delivery is charged on top (NZD 7 to 78 for online applications, by destination).

processingDays.note: DIA advises allowing at least 4 weeks (20 working days, converted to 28 calendar days) for processing, and adding time for delivery; a working day excludes weekends, public holidays and the Christmas/New Year break. A DIA statement reported 85.6% of passports issued within 10 working days in one week. Urgent service: aim to process within 3 working days (converted to 3-5 calendar days), depending on demand; urgent adult passport total NZD 494 and urgent child NZD 391, i.e. the NZD 247 surcharge on top of the base fee, which is also the cost to upgrade an existing application. Urgent applicants collecting at a DIA counter pay no courier.

childValidityNote: Adult passports (age 16 and over) are valid up to 10 years; child passports (under 16) up to 5 years. Child passport fee NZD 144 (from 2 May 2025).

lostReplacement.note: The lost/stolen/damaged passport is declared (online or form PAS201) and cancelled with an alert on the holder's record; a still-valid stolen passport must be reported to police with the report number given. A new passport is not issued until the holder applies for one. No separate lost-passport fee was found.

abroadNote: Citizens overseas apply online to DIA (overseas paper forms go to offices in New Zealand, Sydney or London, paid in local currency). Fees are the same NZD amounts; non-residents for NZ tax applying online are not charged GST. Courier delivery NZD 7 to 78 depending on country. An emergency travel document for returning home costs NZD 685.

issuer: Pilsonības un migrācijas lietu pārvalde (Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs, PMLP/OCMA), under the Ministry of the Interior
docName: Latvijas Republikas pilsoņa pase (Latvian citizen's passport)

fee.feeBasis: State fee for issuing a passport within 10 working days, from 1 January 2026 (Cabinet Regulation No. 133 of 21.02.2012, as amended). The same fee applies to a first passport and a replacement. Apply in person at any PMLP division; there is no online channel. Reduced fee of €25 for people under 20, pension-age or pensioner holders, and group I/II disability. The passport is optional in Latvia; the eID card (€30) is the mandatory identity document from age 15. Expedite: €75 is the full state fee for issue within 2 working days (not a surcharge); the reduced category pays €45. 2 working days x7/5 = 2.8, rounded to 3 calendar days. Express is charged at the 10-day rate for: a surname change within 30 days of marriage; within 30 days of naturalisation; medical treatment abroad; travel for a relative's illness or death; and under-20s or students under 24 on an organised school or youth trip.

processingDays.note: 10 working days x7/5 = 14 calendar days, counted from when the state fee payment reaches the State Treasury. Collection is in person at the division. No minimum is stated.

childValidityNote: Validity by age: under 5, 2 years or the duration of the trip; 5 to 20, 5 years; from 20, 10 years. The 10-year adult validity applies from age 20, not 18.

lostReplacement.note: The loss must be reported at once to PMLP, the State Police, the State Border Guard or, abroad, a Latvian mission. A document reported lost in writing becomes invalid even if found. Without another valid ID, the new application is due within 30 days. The fee schedule has no loss-specific fee, so the ordinary state fee applies. Losing a personal identification document can bring a warning or a fine of up to 14 fine units (€70) under Section 17(4) of the Personal Identification Documents Law.

abroadNote: Abroad, apply in person at a Latvian embassy or consulate, which charges its own consular fees. Example, the Embassy of Latvia in Ireland (page updated 15.07.2026): adult passport €140 on the normal track (about 5 weeks on average) or €165 urgent (about 3 weeks); under-20s, pensioners and group I/II disability pay €115 or €135; forwarding documents within the consular district costs €15. A mission can issue a temporary travel document to return to Latvia if the passport is lost abroad.
